page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 223 GB local SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.i1.xlarge sits in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, both stress-ng single-core and multi-core performance are categorized in the bottom 25% (weak). Similarly, Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the weak category. Cryptographic and integer operations are supported by hardware flags such as AES, AVX, AVX512F, BMI2, and FMA, though overall processing capabilities remain modest.

Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with large-block read operations falling into the bottom 10% (poor) and write operations in the bottom 25% (weak). The local 223 GB SSD provides direct storage, but database operations and Redis SET benchmarks are limited, scoring in the bottom 10%. Static web serving throughput is also constrained at 2.5 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested instances.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.i1.xlarge is positioned as a general-purpose instance with local storage. However, due to its weak benchmark profile across compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations, it is best suited for low-intensity workloads, basic development environments, or legacy applications that require dedicated CPU cores and local SSD storage without demanding high throughput or rapid data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance equipped with an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 16.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 223 GB local SSD. Network performance is limited to a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers weak to poor performance across CPU, memory bandwidth, and database operations, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and Redis SET operations all scoring in the bottom 25% or lower. While the dedicated CPU allocation and local SSD offer resource isolation and direct storage, the overall processing and memory throughput are constrained. Consequently, this instance is best suited for low-demand general-purpose workloads, basic file hosting, or development environments that require dedicated resources but do not demand high computational or transactional performance.
